title: Faulty algorithm worksheet and test plan template
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Think like a computer: algorithms
source: Seeded from computing/y7 lesson 9 (Faulty algorithm worksheet and test plan template (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 9: Testing and debugging algorithms; unit quiz. To understand how testing with normal, boundary and invalid data finds errors in an algorithm

model.title: IF score > 50 THEN OUTPUT 'Pass' ELSE OUTPUT 'Fail'. Test with 50.

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Actual: Fail, so there is a logic error

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: Fix: IF score >= 50; re-test 50 gives Pass

questions.q: Give normal, boundary and invalid data for 'enter a month number 1 to 12'.
questions.model: Teacher writes the range on a number line and marks the edges 1 and 12, then picks a middle value and a nonsense value.

questions.q: Find the bug: 'FOR i = 1 TO 10: OUTPUT i' should output 1 to 9.
questions.a: The loop runs to 10; change to FOR i = 1 TO 9.

questions.q: Core: Write a test plan (4 tests) for the password-lock flowchart from last lesson.
questions.a: Correct first time; wrong then right; 3 wrong (locked); empty password.
questions.model: Teacher writes test 1: 'Input correct password first time; expected: Welcome'.

questions.q: Extend: Trace the faulty algorithm on the worksheet and fix its logic error.
questions.a: The counter is never increased, so it never locks; add tries = tries + 1.

questions.q: Unit quiz (portal secure test mode, 10 questions): algorithms, decomposition, abstraction, building blocks, flowcharts, testing.
Big question: which score would you test first for a pass mark of 50, and why?
questions.a: 50, because it is the boundary where > and >= give different results.
